title.zh: 无知之幕 · 平均原则与最大最小原则
title.en: The veil of ignorance · average rule vs maximin

description.zh: 如果在不知道自己会是谁时挑选社会规则，海萨尼说应选平均福祉最高的社会（每个位置机会均等），罗尔斯说这种一次性、改不了的选择应先保证最差的位置（最大最小原则）；风险态度越保守，选择就越从前者滑向后者。
description.en: Choosing society’s rules without knowing who you will be, Harsanyi says pick the society with the highest average welfare (each position equally likely), while Rawls says such a one-shot, irreversible choice should first secure the worst position (maximin); the more risk-averse the chooser, the more the choice slides from the first towards the second.

label.en: The average rule is an expected value

reason.zh: 海萨尼假设落到每个位置的概率相等，于是比较各社会的平均福祉——正是对位置取期望值；罗尔斯的反驳则是：一生只抽一次，期望值未必是该看的数。
reason.en: Harsanyi assumes every position is equally likely and so compares average welfare — the expected value over positions; Rawls replies that with only one draw in a lifetime, the expected value is not necessarily the number to look at.
